def: A pattern where the system searches a document collection at query time and puts the best passages into the prompt so the model answers from evidence instead of memory.
A passage of a document, usually a few hundred tokens, that is embedded and retrieved as one unit.
A map from each term to the list of documents that contain it, which lets keyword search touch only the documents sharing a query term.
A keyword score that multiplies how often a term appears in a document by the log of how rare it is across the collection.
The standard keyword ranking function: TF-IDF with saturating term frequency (k1) and document length normalisation (b).
Search that embeds query and documents as vectors and returns the documents whose vectors are most similar to the query vector.
A retriever model that embeds query and document separately, so document vectors can be precomputed and searched quickly.
A model that reads a query and a document together and outputs one relevance score; more accurate than a bi-encoder but too slow to run over a whole collection.
Search that returns probably-the-nearest vectors while examining only a small fraction of the collection, trading a little recall for large speed-ups.
An inverted-file vector index that clusters vectors with k-means and searches only the nprobe clusters nearest to the query.
A graph-based vector index with layers of proximity graphs; search walks greedily from sparse top layers down to the full bottom layer, at roughly logarithmic cost.
A compression method that splits each vector into sub-vectors and stores only the index of the nearest centroid for each, shrinking vectors by 30 times or more.
The fraction of relevant items that appear in the top k results; in RAG, whether the evidence reached the prompt.
Running keyword and embedding retrieval together and merging their results, since each finds queries the other misses.
A way to merge ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) for each document across lists, with k usually 60; it needs no score normalisation.
Rescoring a short candidate list from fast retrieval with a slower, more accurate model, then keeping the best few.
Hypothetical Document Embeddings: embedding an LLM-written hypothetical answer instead of the question, to search in answer-shaped space.
A RAG variant that builds an entity-relation graph and community summaries from the documents to answer relational and corpus-wide questions.
The fraction of claims in an answer that are supported by the retrieved context.
The fraction of the facts needed for a complete answer that appear in the retrieved context.
